name: paper-ingest
description: Fetch one paper or long article and land it in knowledge as a citable reference: three specialist passes in parallel — digest, claims, identity — one grounding check, one write, on a fixed four-model-call budget. The host must be on your egress allow-list first.

paper_url.help: The paper or article to read. Its host must already be listed under Settings → Security → Allowed Egress Hosts — automated fetches use an EXCLUSIVE allow-list, so an unlisted host is refused before any request leaves the machine.

reading_goal.help: Why you are reading it — "does this beat our current retrieval approach", "is the evaluation trustworthy". Left empty you get a neutral digest; given a goal, the digest is written against it.

metadata.why_four_calls: Exactly four model calls per paper, and the number is a design invariant rather than an outcome: one reasoning-tier digest, two fast-tier extractions beside it, and one judge. The fetch and the write are zero-token actions, and the three passes run concurrently — so ingesting a paper costs a bounded, predictable amount however long the paper is.
metadata.why_three_passes_not_one: Summarising, extracting checkable claims, and reading bibliographic identity off the front matter are three different jobs with three different output shapes. One prompt asked for all three optimises for a single coherent answer and does the mechanical two badly — and it would pay reasoning-tier prices for work the fast tier does correctly.
metadata.egress_is_the_consent_surface: `net-fetch` reaches nothing until the paper's host sits in `security.egress.allow_hosts`. With an empty list the first run FAILS by design, naming the host and the exact setting — that refusal is how the user grants the reach, and this template has no way to widen it.
metadata.bounded_by_the_provider_not_the_paper: No `max_chars` is declared, so the fetch takes the provider's own 20,000-character ceiling. A paper longer than that arrives truncated and the passes are told so — a digest written as though it saw a whole paper it only saw the front of is the failure this template refuses to hide.

steering_examples.description: Read this retrieval paper and file it — I care most about whether their evaluation actually supports the headline claim.
The claims pass is recording the abstract's marketing sentences as claims — only take assertions the paper offers evidence for.

example_outputs: one citable reference item holding the digest, its checkable claims, and the bibliographic details, retrievable by the questions it answers
metadata.when_not_to_use: not for a page you want to keep re-reading as it changes — that is dual-sink-watcher; and not for raw text you already have, which is rich-ingest

children.label: Read the paper through the egress guard
Three specialists on the same text
Pass 1 — what it says and what it is worth
Pass 3 — who wrote it, where, when
Is every claim and detail in the paper?
File it as a citable reference
